Prof '''Robert William Pringle''' OBE [[FRSE]] [[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] [[Institute of Physics|FIP]] [[American Physical Society|FAPS]] (2 May 1920&ndash;20 June 1996) was a 20th-century Scottish physicist.

==Life==
He was born in [[Edinburgh]] on 2 May 1920 the son of Llllias Dalgleish Hair and her husband, Robert Pringle. He was educated at [[George Heriot's School]] then studied physics at the [[University of Edinburgh]], gaining the Vans Dunlop scholarship and graduated with a BSc in 1942. After graduation he assisted in University lectures. In 1945 he took up the post of lecturer under [[Norman Feather|Professor Norman Feather]].

In 1948 he left Edinburgh to go to Canada as assistant professor of physics at the [[University of Manitoba]] becoming a full professor in 1951, aged 31. He left there in 1955 to return to the UK where he took on the role as Chairman of Nuclear Enterprises (UK) Ltd. There he won the [[Queen's Award to Industry]] twice and won the [[Design Council]] Award for the diagnostic ultrasound scanner.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rse.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/obits_alpha/pringle_robert.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2018-01-22 |archive-date=2018-01-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180122235104/https://www.rse.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/obits_alpha/pringle_robert.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1964 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]. His proposers were [[James Kyles]], [[Norman Feather]], [[Douglas Haig McIntosh]], and [[George Richard Evans]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Biographical Index of Former Fellows of the Royal Society of Edinburgh 1783–2002|date=July 2006|publisher=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|isbn=0-902-198-84-X|url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/biographical_index/fells_indexp2.pdf|access-date=2018-01-22|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304074135/https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/biographical_index/fells_indexp2.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He died on 10 June 1996.

==Family==

In 1948 he married Carol. They had one daughter and three sons. He was older brother to Derek Hair Pringle [[FRSE]] (1926–1995).

==Publications==
*''The Gamma Rays from Neutron-Activated Gold'' (1950)
*''20th Century Scottish Banknotes'' (1984) with James Douglas
